Massive Hollywood movies changed by the CIA and Pentagon may look like ordinary entertainment, but behind the scenes, government agencies have helped rewrite scripts, remove uncomfortable details, provide military equipment, and block productions that refused to cooperate.

This countdown explores how movies such as Top Gun, Transformers, Captain Marvel, Zero Dark Thirty, The Recruit, Patriot Games, and even Meet the Parents were influenced by official government advisers. It also reveals why the Pentagon withdrew support from Thirteen Days, Platoon, Forrest Gump, and other films that portrayed military failures, war crimes, or controversial operations too honestly.
From CIA liaison Chase Brandon shaping heroic intelligence agents to the military providing millions of dollars in aircraft, ships, bases, and personnel, Hollywood receives valuable access in exchange for creative control.
